import java.io.*;
import java.util.*;

public class C {
    public static void main(String[] args) throws Exception {
        C program = new C();
        program.runProgram();
    }
    
    public void runProgram() throws Exception {
        BufferedReader br = new BufferedReader(new InputStreamReader(System.in));
        String[] parts = br.readLine().trim().split("\\s+");
        int n = Integer.parseInt(parts[0]);
        double d = Double.parseDouble(parts[1]);
        
        // Handle edge cases
        if (n < 3) {
            // If n < 3, the game cannot be played as described
            // But per problem constraints, n >= 3 likely
            System.out.println(0);
            return;
        }
        
        for (int i = 0; i <= n; i++) {
            double prob = calculateProbability(n, i);
            
            if (prob + 1e-12 >= d) {
                System.out.println(i);
                return;
            }
        }
        
        System.out.println(n);
    }
    
    private double calculateProbability(int n, int studied) {
        if (studied == 0) return 0.0;
        if (studied == n) return 1.0;
        
        // Total ways to choose 3 maps from n
        long total = (long)n * (n-1) * (n-2);
        
        // Count favorable cases where at least one of the studied maps is selected
        // and not discarded by both players
        
        // Case 1: Exactly 1 studied map in the 3 shown
        // - Both players must NOT discard it (each has 2/3 chance to discard one of the other 2)
        // - The system picks randomly among non-discarded maps
        // Probability that the studied map is played: 
        //   P(1 studied in 3) * P(both players don't discard it) * P(it gets selected)
        //   + P(1 studied in 3) * P(one discards it, one doesn't) * P(it gets selected)
        //   + P(1 studied in 3) * P(both discard it) * 0
        
        // Actually, let's think more carefully:
        // We have 3 maps: S (studied) and U1, U2 (unstudied)
        // Each player independently picks one to discard
        // System then picks randomly from maps not discarded by anyone
        
        // For a single studied map case:
        // - If both players discard the same map (could be S or U1 or U2):
        //   * If they discard S: S is not played
        //   * If they discard U1: S and U2 remain, S played with prob 1/2
        //   * If they discard U2: S and U1 remain, S played with prob 1/2
        
        // Let's enumerate all 9 combinations (each player has 3 choices):
        // Players pick from {S, U1, U2}
        
        // Case: both pick S -> discard S -> S not played (0)
        // Case: player1 picks S, player2 picks U1 -> discard S and U1 -> only U2 remains -> S not played (0)
        // Case: player1 picks S, player2 picks U2 -> discard S and U2 -> only U1 remains -> S not played (0)
        // Case: player1 picks U1, player2 picks S -> discard U1 and S -> only U2 remains -> S not played (0)
        // Case: both pick U1 -> discard U1 -> S and U2 remain -> S played with prob 1/2
        // Case: player1 picks U1, player2 picks U2 -> discard U1 and U2 -> only S remains -> S played (1)
        // Case: player1 picks U2, player2 picks S -> discard U2 and S -> only U1 remains -> S not played (0)
        // Case: player1 picks U2, player2 picks U1 -> discard U2 and U1 -> only S remains -> S played (1)
        // Case: both pick U2 -> discard U2 -> S and U1 remain -> S played with prob 1/2
        
        // So for 1 studied map in 3 shown:
        // P(S played) = (1/9)*0 + (1/9)*0 + (1/9)*0 + (1/9)*0 + (1/9)*(1/2) + (1/9)*1 + (1/9)*0 + (1/9)*1 + (1/9)*(1/2)
        //             = 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 1/18 + 1/9 + 0 + 1/9 + 1/18
        //             = 1/18 + 2/18 + 2/18 + 1/18 = 6/18 = 1/3
        
        // Case: Exactly 2 studied maps in 3 shown (S1, S2) and 1 unstudied (U)
        // Players pick from {S1, S2, U}
        // We want P(at least one studied map is played)
        
        // Actually, let's compute P(no studied map is played) = P(only U is played)
        // U is played only if both players discard both S1 and S2
        // That means both players must pick either S1 or S2 to discard
        // P(both discard S1) = 1/9, both discard S2 = 1/9, player1 S1 player2 S2 = 1/9, player1 S2 player2 S1 = 1/9
        // In all these cases, U remains. But if both discard the same (S1 or S2), then U and the other studied remain.
        // If they discard different studied maps, only U remains.
        
        // So P(U is the only remaining) = 2/9 (when they pick different studied maps)
        // In that case, U is played for sure.
        // P(only one studied remains) = 2/9 (both discard S1, or both discard S2)
        // In that case, the remaining studied is played for sure.
        // P(both studied remain) = 5/9 (various combinations where at least one studied isn't discarded by anyone)
        // In that case, system picks randomly between the two studied maps, so P(studied played) = 1
        
        // Actually, if both studied remain, system picks randomly between them, so P(studied played) = 1
        // If one studied remains, that studied is played for sure, so P(studied played) = 1
        // If no studied remains (only U), P(studied played) = 0
        
        // So P(studied played) = 1 - P(only U remains) = 1 - 2/9 = 7/9
        
        // Case: All 3 maps are studied
        // Then P(studied played) = 1
        
        // Now compute overall probability:
        // P(exactly 1 studied in 3) = C(studied, 1) * C(n-studied, 2) / C(n, 3)
        // P(exactly 2 studied in 3) = C(studied, 2) * C(n-studied, 1) / C(n, 3)
        // P(exactly 3 studied in 3) = C(studied, 3) / C(n, 3)
        
        long c_n_3 = (long)n * (n-1) * (n-2) / 6;
        long c_s_1 = studied;
        long c_ns_2 = (long)(n - studied) * (n - studied - 1) / 2;
        long c_s_2 = (long)studied * (studied - 1) / 2;
        long c_ns_1 = n - studied;
        long c_s_3 = (long)studied * (studied - 1) * (studied - 2) / 6;
        
        double p1 = (double)(c_s_1 * c_ns_2) / c_n_3;  // exactly 1 studied
        double p2 = (double)(c_s_2 * c_ns_1) / c_n_3;  // exactly 2 studied
        double p3 = (double)c_s_3 / c_n_3;             // exactly 3 studied
        
        return p1 * (1.0/3.0) + p2 * (7.0/9.0) + p3 * 1.0;
    }
}
